title: How to Run Your First AI Engineering Project
coverHeadline:
How to Run
Your First
[[AI Engineering]]
Project
hookStatement: You build a quick AI demo, it works on the first try, and everyone is excited. Then real users show up, and the answers start drifting in ways nobody can explain.
industryTension: Most of us start by picking the most popular model and writing a long prompt. The trouble is that without tests, every small tweak can quietly break something that used to work, and you won't know until a user tells you.
architecturalFramework: Here's what experienced teams do instead: they write a small set of tests first, lock the output into a schema, start with the simplest setup that could work, set a budget for speed and cost, log every call, and keep a fallback ready for when the model misbehaves.
goldenRule: If a few lines of code and one well-written prompt can solve it, you probably don't need an agent yet. Add complexity only when your tests show you need it.
takeawayAndCta: The model is the easy part. The system you build around it is what makes it reliable. Pick one feature this week and write ten test cases for it first. Save this for later and follow @yvnalvworks for more. yvnalvworks.com/projects
evidenceSources: Huyen, Chip. 'AI Engineering: Building Applications with Foundation Models' (O'Reilly, 2024)
